details: CONFIRMED on the live records. earlier_records() takes the newest HISTORY=5 files whatever they are, and dropped()
pools them. The 2026-10-25T02 record is a partial batch (partial: true, 13 meaning and 39 code graders failed, a
broken branch): it drags the baseline of every case it holds down for the next five waves, so a real fall right after
it is hidden. The queue item's pass case "a case whose rate over its last runs drops below its earlier rate is named"
and its promise "a fault that hits 1 run in 3 is still seen" are not met on the very case that started the item.
A red but complete record may be argued either way; a partial one is by definition not a measured batch.
Size: 10 agent minutes.
failing_case: Stored records for no-spec-step-typo, oldest first: 2026-10-25T02-29-53Z (partial: true, 0 of 3), 2026-10-26T01 (3 of 3),
Now: dropped() for 2026-10-27T07 against its 5 earlier records returns [] (earlier pooled 6 of 9 = 2/3, not below);
for aa8cfd1 returns [] (8 of 12 = 2/3). The case the queue item names as the new 1-in-3 fault is never reported as falling.
Should: both name no-spec-step-typo ("pass rate fell to 2 of 3 runs"); with partial records left out of the baseline
they do (earlier 6/6 and 8/9).
fix_hint: In earlier_records (or dropped), skip records with "partial" true, taking the newest HISTORY complete records; add the
pass_cases: 1. earlier = [partial batch with case c 0 of 3, batch c 3 of 3, batch c 3 of 3]; now c 2 of 3 -> report names "c: pass rate fell to 2 of 3".
2. earlier = [batch c 3 of 3]; now c 2 of 3 -> named (works today, test_a_falling_rate_is_named).
3. earlier = [batch c 2 of 3]; now c 2 of 3 -> not named (works today).
4. no earlier records -> not named (works today).
5. main() with RELAY_HOME holding a partial record and a full record of c 3 of 3, new c 2 of 3 -> output names the fall.
findings.summary: the falling-rate baseline pools partial (broken) records, so the live no-spec-step-typo fall (2 of 3 twice) is never named

details: Question for the owner. How it works: an eval run that hits the time or turn limit has no grader results; the change
keeps the old rule that any not-judged run makes the wave red, and applies the majority only to judged runs. Live
example: 2026-10-27T07 run, keep-owner-words-en runs 1 and 2 timed out after 600 s. (a) keeps a timeout visible as red,
at the cost of a red wave with no regression when one run is slow; (b) treats a timeout like any other failed run,
consistent with "Сценарий проходит с большинством", at the risk of hiding a slow environment until it hits 2 of 3.
Recommendation: (a) until a timeout shows up in a wave that would otherwise be green (not measured as frequent: 0 of 21).
Size: 10 agent minutes if (b).
evidence: read-only script over ~/.relay/evals/relay: 'errored runs 22 files 21'; verdict per record unchanged by this question.
failing_case: A case with runs PASS, PASS, "timed out after 600s": today the wave is RED ("1 not judged"); if a timed-out run counts as
one failed run of three, it would be green by majority. Measured: 22 errored runs in 21 stored records; none of the 21
records changes verdict either way today (2026-10-26T01 design-track and 2026-10-27T07 keep-owner-words-en fail their
majority anyway).
pass_cases: (a) kept as built: PASS, PASS, errored -> RED, "1 not judged".
(b) errored counts as failed: PASS, PASS, errored -> green, note "2 of 3 runs passed"; PASS, errored, errored -> RED.
reason: Owner question already answered (a): timeouts keep the wave red; nothing built, as intended.
findings.summary: owner question: does a timed-out run count as a failed run under the majority, or keep the wave red as not judged
